newsitem.title: USA: US stock index futures end higher, off day's highs.
newsitem.headline: US stock index futures end higher, off day's highs.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended higher, with December Standard & Poor's 500s closing below the daily highs as volume in the pit dried up in the afternoon, traders and analysts said.
"Fund managers threw their money all at once in the morning so they could have the rest of the day off," one floor source said.
He said gains in the futures market were led by the cash market, as fund and money managers continued to re-balance their portfolios in the middle of the month.
Several other traders noted that Chrysler Corp's third-quarter profits, which jumped 92 percent, supported gains in the cash market.
Meanwhile, the Nasdaq composite closed in record high territory, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average ended above the key resistance level of 6,000 for the first time ever.
Traders said December S&Ps were poised to re-test the all-time and contract high of 710.60, which was set last Tuesday, and some targeted 740.00 as the next resistance area.
The contract rose to 709.90, above the contract settlement high of 708.20.
Fair value was at 4.55 points to cash, with arbitrage buy programs at a premium of 5.75 points and arbitrage sell programs at a discount of 3.50 points.
Volume for December S&Ps was estimated at 49,000.

At the end of pit trade, December S&Ps were up 1.60 at 707.50, New Composites were up 0.20 at 375.95, KBT Value Lines were off 0.05 at 651.90, Nikkeis ended an uneventful day up 40.0 at 21,170, Midcap 400s were up 1.25 at 247.45 and Nasdaq 100s rose 4.90 to 779.85.
